narrative.text: Opens a 1992 Bulletin article on the WHO international quality assessment scheme for HIV antibody testing, reporting the second distribution of 20 sera to 103 laboratories in all six WHO regions in 1990. It summarises results: no false negatives for positive specimens, with some false positives and indeterminates for negatives, and concludes that performance was generally good.

Explains the purpose of external quality assessment and the aims of the WHO scheme for HIV antibody testing, then describes the trial and second distributions, specimens, assays and Western blot interpretation criteria. It notes that the 78 laboratories that reported used roughly 70 different assay combinations.
The extracted text of this page is garbled OCR of a large results table, consisting mostly of plus signs and scattered characters with no readable content.

Tables listing the commercial HIV antibody assays used by participating laboratories, the Western blot interpretation criteria they applied, and the combinations of screening and confirmatory assays used.

Presents a table of laboratories' interpretations of each specimen's HIV antibody status, noting that most errors on negative specimens were indeterminate results and were unevenly spread across laboratories. It cautions that quality assessment results cannot be used to compare individual assays because of small and preselected specimen sets.
Tables of Western blot band patterns reported for negative and positive specimens with commercial kits; the extracted text is a largely unreadable jumble of plus and minus signs.

Continues the Western blot table, then discusses the generally high performance of assays under field conditions and the low rates of false results. It explains that quality assessment specimens should be treated like routine samples so that errors can reveal problems in everyday testing.

Stresses that external quality assessment cannot replace internal quality control, considers the 76% response rate satisfactory, and notes that most participants were national reference laboratories, so national schemes are needed to assess other testing sites. A French summary of the article's findings follows.
Ends the French summary, noting variable Western blot profiles and plans to include HIV-2 testing in future distributions, followed by the article's reference list.
